# Commands reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen-docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every operation is a JSON object whose `type` is the operation name, followed by its parameters, e.g.

```json
{"type": "panel.create_rect", "width": 500, "height": 700}
```

IDs are strings such as `"panel:2"`. Lengths are in millimetres.
Errors are structured: a stable `code`, named `args` and an English `text`.

## Script steps

A script (CLI `r3d run`) is a JSON array of steps. A step is a command, a query, or one of:

- `{"type": "history.undo"}`: undo the last step.
- `{"type": "history.redo"}`: redo the last undone step.
- `{"type": "history.list"}`: the steps of the history, oldest first (`steps`, each with its `label`: the command's name, or the batch's), and how many are done (`at`).
- `{"type": "history.go_to", "at": 3}`: undo or redo until `at` steps are done (0 undoes them all).
- `{"type": "batch", "label": "...", "commands": [...]}`: run commands atomically as one undo step, named `label` in the history (optional, default `batch`); if one fails, none is applied.

Undo, redo and go-to return the panels they changed (`panels`); the app selects them.

A string such as `"$3.created[0]"` refers to the result of an earlier step (step 3, 0-based, then the path `.created[0]`; `[n]` indexes arrays, `.name` reads fields). It must be the whole string; `$$` writes a literal `$`. References keep scripts independent of ID allocation.

## Commands

Document edits. Every command can be undone.

### `avatar.set`

Set the avatar's body: masculinity (0 feminine – 1 masculine) and height, bust, waist and hips in cm. The 3D body is fitted to these measurements; avatar.get reports what it actually measures.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Body": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Body measurements (cm), the input of the avatar fitting.",
      "properties": {
        "bust_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "height_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "hips_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "masculinity": {
          "description": "0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine body.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "masculinity",
        "height_cm",
        "bust_cm",
        "waist_cm",
        "hips_cm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the avatar's measurements.",
  "properties": {
    "body": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Body",
      "description": "Measurements in cm; `masculinity` 0 = feminine body, 1 = masculine."
    },
    "preset": {
      "description": "Name of the preset the measurements come from, if any.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "body"
  ],
  "title": "AvatarSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_rect`

Create a rectangular panel. Returns the panel, then its 4 points (counter-clockwise from the origin), then its 4 edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a rectangular panel.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
      "description": "Height in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "origin": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Bottom-left corner on the board, in mm. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "Width in mm (> 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "width",
    "height"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateRect",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_polygon`

Create a panel from a closed polygon. With `symmetric`, the points draw half a piece against an axis, the closing edge: the other half follows (panel.unfold). Returns the panel, then its points, then its edges (then, symmetric, the reflected half's points and edges).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a panel from a closed polygon.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "points": {
      "description": "At least 3 vertices in mm; the closing edge is implicit. Must form a\nsimple outline (no crossing or overlapping edges). Stored\ncounter-clockwise.",
      "items": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "symmetric": {
      "description": "The points draw half a piece: the closing edge, from the last point\nback to the first, is its axis, and the piece is unfolded across it\n(as panel.unfold does).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "points"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreatePolygon",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_path`

Create a panel from a closed path of straight and cubic Bézier edges (mm), like internal_line.add but closed. Must form a simple outline; stored counter-clockwise. With `symmetric`, the path draws half a piece against an axis, the straight edge back to `start`: the other half follows (panel.unfold). Returns the panel, then its points, then its edges (then, symmetric, the reflected half's points and edges).

```json
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [

            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },

              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,

            }
          },
          "required": [

            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a panel from a closed path of straight and curved edges.",
  "properties": {
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"

    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",

      "type": "array"

      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreatePath",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `panel.mirror`

Create a linked mirror copy of a panel (e.g. left/right pieces). The copy follows every later change of its source; move it with panel.translate, or make it independent with panel.unlink. Returns the copy, then its points, then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create a linked mirror copy of a panel.",
  "properties": {
    "axis_dir": {
      "description": "Direction of the mirror axis. Defaults to vertical `[0, 1]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "axis_origin": {
      "description": "A point on the mirror axis (mm). Defaults to a vertical axis placed\nso the copy sits to the right of the source with a 50 mm gap.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Name of the copy. Defaults to \"<source name> (mirror)\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel"
  ],
  "title": "PanelMirror",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.place`

Place a panel around the body (or around an arm, for sleeves) for the 3D simulation: angle (0 front, 90 left side, 180 back, 270 right side; around an arm 0 is its outside), height of its top in cm, distance from the body in mm. Unplaced panels are not simulated.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Around": {
      "description": "What a panel is wrapped around when the simulation starts.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "body",
          "description": "The torso and legs: a vertical cylinder around the body's axis.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_arm",
          "description": "The left arm (the body's left, +x): wrapped around the upper arm,\nthen the forearm past the elbow.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right_arm",
          "description": "The right arm (−x).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "left_leg",
          "description": "The left leg (+x), like a trouser leg: wrapped around the leg's\naxis, and above the crotch around the body's left half.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right_leg",
          "description": "The right leg (−x).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "flat",
          "description": "Not wrapped: a flat sheet facing outward at the placement angle,\n`offset_mm` from the body's vertical axis (a bag hanging in front\nof the body).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place a panel around the body for the simulation.",
  "properties": {
    "angle_deg": {
      "description": "Angle around the body (degrees): 0 front, 90 the body's left side,\n180 back, 270 right side. Around an arm: 0 the outside of the arm,\n180 the side facing the body. Around a leg, as around the body,\ncentred on the leg.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "around": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Around",
      "default": "body",
      "description": "What the panel is wrapped around: `body` (default), `left_arm` or\n`right_arm` (sleeves), `left_leg` or `right_leg` (trouser legs:\naround the leg, and above the crotch around that half of the body),\nor `flat` (not wrapped: a flat sheet facing outward, `offset_mm`\nfrom the body's axis)."
    },
    "centre_x_mm": {
      "description": "The pattern abscissa (mm) that goes to the angle. Defaults to the\npanel's horizontal centre; the pieces of a cut panel keep the\nwhole's.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "offset_mm": {
      "default": 30.0,
      "description": "Distance from the body at the start of the simulation (mm,\ndefault 30). Around an arm or a leg a panel starts as a closed tube\ninstead (around a leg, just outside it if the leg is thicker).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "top_cm": {
      "description": "Height of the panel's top above the floor (cm). Around an arm, the\ntop goes to the arm at that height and the panel runs down the arm.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "angle_deg",
    "top_cm"
  ],
  "title": "PanelPlace",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.cut`

Cut a panel in two along an open path of straight and cubic segments (mm) that crosses its outline exactly twice, its ends outside the panel (without `panel`, the one panel it crosses). The two pieces are sewn together along the cut. The larger piece keeps the panel's ID, its seams and pins; the other is a new panel with the same garment, grain and seam allowance, moved 20 mm away on the board and placed where it was around the body. Notches, internal lines and pins go to the piece they are on; a sewn edge that is cut is split with its partner, and the seam with them. Returns the new panel, then the seams along the cut.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Cut a panel in two along a straight or curved line.",
  "properties": {
    "name": {
      "description": "Name of the new piece. Defaults to the panel's name followed by \" 2\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "panel": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The panel to cut. If omitted, the one panel the line crosses."
    },
    "segments": {
      "description": "The cut line's segments; it ends outside the panel too.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "start": {
      "description": "Start of the cut line (mm), outside the panel.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCut",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.paste`

Paste pieces copied with panel.copy, under new IDs, with the seams between them, their notches, internal lines, grade rules (when the project has the same number of sizes and base size), pins and mirror links. A piece keeps its place around the body unless a piece of the project already starts there (pasted beside its original): then it is left unplaced, with no pins. Returns the new panels, then the new seams.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Paste pieces copied with panel.copy.",
  "properties": {
    "clip": {
      "description": "The clip, as panel.copy returns it."
    },
    "garment": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The garment the pieces join. Omitted: the one they were copied\nfrom if this project has it, otherwise the project's first."
    },
    "offset": {
      "description": "How far to move the pieces on the board (mm). Omitted: to the right\nof the project's pieces.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "clip"
  ],
  "title": "PanelPaste",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `point.set_distance`

Set the straight-line distance between two contour points (e.g. across the shoulders, or between two pieces' corners): `point` moves along the line from `from` through it, as `point.move` does (its curve handles follow); `from` stays. `measure.distance` gives the current distance.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {

    }

  "description": "Put a point at a distance from another.",

}
```

### `seam.add`

Sew two sides together. A side is a whole `edge`, a run of consecutive outline `edges` of one piece (in order around it), or an internal `line`, each optionally only `from_mm`/`to_mm` along it (a seam between two notches, a pocket sewn on its placement line, the two halves of a pleat on one edge). Points are matched along the sides, start to start unless a side is reversed; leave b.reversed out to have it chosen (an edge and its linked mirror image meet mirrored point to mirrored point; other sides are walked both the same way on the pattern), and use seam.flip if the seam looks twisted. Stretches already sewn cannot be sewn again (invalid.overlaps). `ease_mm` is how much longer side a is meant to be. Returns the seam.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "InternalLineId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a line, e.g. `line:1`.",
      "pattern": "^line:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamSideSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One side of a new seam: a whole edge, a run of edges, or an internal\nline; all of it or part of it.",
      "properties": {
        "edge": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "One edge."
        },
        "edges": {
          "description": "Or consecutive outline edges of one piece, in their order around it\n(e.g. a pocket's sides and bottom).",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "from_mm": {
          "description": "Only from here along the path (mm from its start). Omitted: its\nstart.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "line": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/InternalLineId"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Or an internal line (a pocket's placement line, a tuck's line)."
        },
        "reversed": {
          "description": "Walk the side from its end instead of its start. Omitted: `false`\nfor side `a`; for side `b`, an edge sewn to its linked mirror image\nmeets it mirrored point to mirrored point (a centre seam), other\nsides are walked both the same way on the pattern (what sewing two\npanels laid side by side needs).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "to_mm": {
          "description": "Only to here (mm from the path's start). Omitted: its end.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Sew two sides together.",
  "properties": {
    "a": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "b": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamSideSpec"
    },
    "ease_mm": {
      "description": "How much longer side `a` is meant to be than `b` (mm, negative:\nshorter), eased in: not reported as a mismatch.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "title": "SeamAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `dart.add`

Draw a dart on an outline edge, fold it and sew it, in one step: the edge is opened `width_mm` wide around `at_mm`, the dart's point goes `length_mm` into the piece, and its two legs are sewn together (the cloth closes when it drapes). Returns the dart's point, its two legs and the seam. Constraints on the edge are removed.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a dart on an edge.",
  "properties": {
    "at_mm": {
      "description": "Where the dart's middle is along the edge (mm from its start).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "How far into the piece its point is (mm, > 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "width_mm": {
      "description": "How much the dart takes in at the edge (mm, > 0).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "at_mm",
    "width_mm",
    "length_mm"
  ],
  "title": "DartAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `pleat.add`

Fold and sew a pleat on an outline edge (a skirt's waist): from `at_mm`, a knife pleat folds `depth_mm` of cloth under (the edge's stretch of 2 × depth is sewn to itself, folded in the middle), a box pleat two such folds facing away from each other; with `stitched_mm`, the folds are also stitched down that far into the piece (along internal lines). Notches mark the fold lines. Returns the seams, then the lines and notches.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PleatKind": {
      "description": "How a pleat folds.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "knife",
          "description": "One fold, all the same way.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "box",
          "description": "Two folds facing away from each other.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a pleat on an edge.",
  "properties": {
    "at_mm": {
      "description": "Where the pleat starts along the edge (mm from its start).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "depth_mm": {
      "description": "How deep each fold is (mm, > 0): a knife pleat takes up twice that\nalong the edge, a box pleat four times.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "kind": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PleatKind",
      "default": "knife"
    },
    "stitched_mm": {
      "description": "Stitched down this far into the piece (mm); 0 or omitted: held at\nthe edge only.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "at_mm",
    "depth_mm"
  ],
  "title": "PleatAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.add_hole`

Cut a hole in a piece (a buttonhole opening, a cut-out): a closed path of straight and cubic edges (mm) inside the piece, not crossing its outline or its other holes. The hole is left out of the cloth; its edges can be sewn and notched like the outline's. Returns the hole's points, then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Cut a hole in a piece.",
  "properties": {
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    },
    "segments": {
      "description": "Its edges in order (straight or cubic), back to `start` (a straight\nedge closes it otherwise).",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "start": {
      "description": "First point of the hole's outline (mm).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "start",
    "segments"
  ],
  "title": "PanelAddHole",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.boolean`

Join two overlapping pieces into one (`union`), or cut a piece with another (`difference`: a bite out of its outline, or a hole when the other lies inside it). The result is fitted with straight and curved edges; the other piece is removed unless `keep`. Pieces that are sewn, symmetric or mirrored must be unpicked or unlinked first; notches on the changed outline go. Fails if the result would be several pieces or nothing.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "BooleanOp": {
      "description": "What a boolean keeps.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "union",
          "description": "Both pieces' cloth: one piece (they must overlap or touch).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "difference",
          "description": "The first piece without the second: a notch cut in its outline, or\na hole when the second lies inside.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Join two pieces into one, or cut one with another.",
  "properties": {
    "keep": {
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "op": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/BooleanOp"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId",
      "description": "The piece changed."
    },
    "with": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId",
      "description": "The other piece: joined to `panel` (`union`), or cut out of it\n(`difference`). It goes, unless `keep`."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "with",
    "op"
  ],
  "title": "PanelBoolean",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.lengthen`

Lengthen (mm > 0) or shorten (mm < 0) the garment at an open edge such as a hem: the edge moves along its panel's grain, and so do the edges it continues into across seams (the whole hemline), so sewn sides stay matched. Linked mirror copies follow their source.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Move an open edge, and the line it continues across seams, along the\ngrain.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "An open (unsewn) edge: a hem, a sleeve end, a neckline."
    },
    "mm": {
      "description": "How far to move it (mm): positive makes the garment longer.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeLengthen",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.set_length`

Give an edge a new length (mm): it is scaled about its middle, curve included, so its end points move along it. A sewn edge's partner is scaled in the same ratio so the seam stays matched, and so are the symmetric seams of linked mirror copies (which follow their source).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Scale an edge about its middle to a given length.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "The new length along the edge (mm).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "length_mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeSetLength",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `seam.take_in`

Take in (mm > 0) or let out (mm < 0) a seam: both sides move inward by half of mm, perpendicular to the seam, so they stay matched. With `at` (an end point of the seam) only that end moves, tapering the change (e.g. take in the waist only). With linked mirror copies the symmetric seam is taken in too, so every seam stays matched.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a seam, e.g. `seam:1`.",
      "pattern": "^seam:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Take in (mm > 0) or let out (mm < 0) a seam.",
  "properties": {
    "at": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "An end point of the seam (on either side) to take in at that end\nonly, tapering to nothing at the other end. Omitted: the whole seam."
    },
    "mm": {
      "description": "Total width taken in (mm): each side moves half of it inward.\nNegative lets the seam out.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "seam": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "seam",
    "mm"
  ],
  "title": "SeamTakeIn",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `seam.match_length`

Make the two sides of a seam the same length: the side other than `keep` is scaled about its middle to `keep`'s length (on a linked mirror copy, its source is). Afterwards `edge.set_length` keeps them equal.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SeamId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a seam, e.g. `seam:1`.",
      "pattern": "^seam:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Make a seam's other side as long as `keep`.",
  "properties": {
    "keep": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "The side that keeps its length: one of the seam's two edges."
    },
    "seam": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SeamId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "seam",
    "keep"
  ],
  "title": "SeamMatchLength",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

Pin the cloth: the panel's cloth within 3 cm of `at` (pattern mm) is held still at `position` (3D metres) during the simulation. Returns the pin.

```json
}
```

### `garment.arrange`

Place every panel around the body for the simulation, side by side in the order the seams join them (a panel's right side continues into the next panel; each takes a share of the turn in proportion to its width), tops at the avatar's waist (its narrowest girth) unless top_cm is given. Panels placed on an arm (sleeves) or flat keep their placement. Re-run it after adding panels or seams.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Place every panel around the body.",

      "description": "Height of the panels' tops (cm). Default: the avatar's waist.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "GarmentArrange",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "GarmentId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a garment, e.g. `garment:1`.",
      "pattern": "^garment:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Move a piece to another garment.",
  "properties": {
    "garment": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/GarmentId"
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "garment"
  ],
  "title": "PanelSetGarment",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `grading.set_sizes`

Set the project's size range: the sizes from smallest to largest, each with how its body differs from the base size's (the avatar; cm), and the base size the pattern is drawn in. Garments drafted from a template and not graded yet are graded by drafting the template for every size's body. Points keep their grade in the sizes that stay (by name); new sizes are inter- or extrapolated. Changing the base redraws the pattern in that size. See grading.use_chart for standard sizes.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SizeSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One size of a range, as commands take it.",
      "properties": {
        "bust_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "height_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "description": "How the size's body differs from the base size's (cm; default 0).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "hips_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "name": {
          "description": "As on the label: \"38\", \"M\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "waist_cm": {
          "default": 0.0,
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "name"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the project's size range.",
  "properties": {
    "base": {
      "description": "The size the pattern is drawn in (a name from `sizes`).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "From the smallest to the largest; at least two, names unique.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/SizeSpec"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "sizes",
    "base"
  ],
  "title": "GradingSetSizes",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `grading.use_chart`

Set the project's size range from a built-in European chart (`women` 32–56, `men` 44–60, every second size): the sizes from `from` to `to`, drawn in `base`. Each size's body differs from the avatar as the chart's sizes differ from its base size; without an avatar, the chart's base body becomes the avatar. Garments drafted from a template, before or after, are graded to every size; grade other points with point.set_grade.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "SizeChart": {
      "description": "A built-in size chart.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "women",
          "description": "European women's sizes 32 to 56 (bust 76–134 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "men",
          "description": "European men's sizes 44 to 60 (chest 88–120 cm).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set the size range from a built-in chart.",
  "properties": {
    "base": {
      "description": "The size the pattern is drawn in, e.g. \"40\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "chart": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/SizeChart",
      "description": "`women` (32–56) or `men` (44–60)."
    },
    "from": {
      "description": "Smallest size of the range, e.g. \"36\".",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "to": {
      "description": "Largest size, e.g. \"52\".",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "chart",
    "from",
    "to",
    "base"
  ],
  "title": "GradingUseChart",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `grading.clear`

Remove the size range and every point's grade: the pattern stays in its base size. Destructive: requires "confirm": true.

**Destructive**: requires `"confirm": true`.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
```

### `point.set_grade`

Set how a contour point moves from size to size (its grade rule): either `step`, the same move from each size to the next (mm, [x, y]; e.g. [5, 0] moves the point 5 mm outward per size), or `offsets`, where it is in some sizes relative to the base size, the others inter- or extrapolated. A zero step removes the rule. Curve handles, internal lines and pins follow the points; linked mirror copies follow their source, mirrored.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Set a point's grade rule.",
  "properties": {
    "offsets": {
      "additionalProperties": {
        "items": {
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "type": "array"
      },
      "description": "Or where the point is in some sizes, from its base position (mm,\nby size name); the other sizes are inter- or extrapolated.",
      "type": [
        "object",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
    },
    "step": {
      "description": "The same move from each size to the next (mm, [x, y]).",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "point"
  ],
  "title": "PointSetGrade",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `template.apply`

Draft a starter garment (t_shirt, shirt, trousers, dress, straight_skirt, a_line_skirt, tote_bag) from sizes in cm, the avatar's measurements filling in any left out: its pieces are drawn, sewn, placed around the body and given a fabric, ready to simulate and edit. A project without panels takes the template's name, and so does its garment; in a project with pieces the template becomes a garment of its own, worn over the others (see garment.set_layer). Returns the garment if one was added, then the panels, seams and notches.

### `pattern.import`

Add pattern pieces in one step: for each, its sewing line (as in panel.create_path), seam allowance, grainline angle, notches (points near the outline) and internal lines. Placed to the right of the existing pieces unless keep_position. `import.pattern` reads them from a DXF, SVG or PDF file. Returns, for each piece, its panel, points and edges, then its notches and lines.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "LineSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "An open path (mm).",
      "properties": {
        "segments": {
          "description": "At least one segment.",

            "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },

          "items": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "maxItems": 2,
          "minItems": 2,
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "start",
        "segments"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PieceSpec": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "One piece of an imported pattern.",
      "properties": {
        "grain_angle_deg": {
          "default": 90.0,
          "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X (default 90, vertical).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "internal_lines": {
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/LineSpec"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "name": {
          "description": "Piece name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "notches": {
          "description": "Notches: points on or near the outline (within 5 mm), each put on\nthe nearest edge.",
          "items": {
            "items": {
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "maxItems": 2,
            "minItems": 2,
            "type": "array"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "seam_allowance_mm": {
          "description": "Seam allowance in mm (default 0).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "segments": {
          "description": "…and the edges in order; the last should end at `start`.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/SegmentSpec"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "start": {
          "description": "The sewing line, as in `panel.create_path`: first point (mm)…",
          "items": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "maxItems": 2,
          "minItems": 2,
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "start",
        "segments"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SegmentSpec": {
      "description": "One segment of an internal line, starting where the previous one ended.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "line",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {
            "c1": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "c2": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cubic",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "items": {
                "format": "double",
                "type": "number"
              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,
              "type": "array"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "c1",
            "c2",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add the pieces of a pattern made elsewhere.",
  "properties": {
    "keep_position": {
      "description": "Keep the given coordinates. By default the pieces are moved, all\ntogether, to the right of the pieces already on the board.",
      "type": "boolean"
```

### `constraint.add`

Add a constraint (fixed, coincident, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal_length, on_edge) or a dimension (distance, length, angle) on contour points and edges. A dimension with a `formula` (e.g. "waist / 4 + 10 mm") takes its value from the body's measurements and the variables, now and whenever they change, and in every size of the range. The drawing is solved at once: the geometry moves as little as possible so that every constraint holds; constraints that cannot all hold are refused (`constraints_unsolvable`). With `measure`, a dimension keeps the value it has now. Returns the constraint; `constraint.list` shows them with the freedom left.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Along": {
      "description": "How a distance is measured.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "direct",
          "description": "In a straight line.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "horizontal",
          "description": "Across: the difference of the two points' x.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "vertical",
          "description": "Up or down: the difference of their y.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "Constraint": {
      "description": "A relation the drawing keeps between points and edges: after every\nchange, the constraint solver moves the geometry so that all of them\nhold again (`docs/specs/19-constraints.md`). Dimensions (`distance`,\n`length`, `angle`) carry a value; the others are geometric.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The point never moves when the solver adjusts the drawing (it moves\nonly when it is moved itself).",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "fixed",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "point": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "point"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Two points at the same place (on two pieces, usually).",
          "properties": {
            "a": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
            },
            "b": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "coincident",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "a",
            "b"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The edge's ends at the same height.",
          "properties": {
            "edge": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "horizontal",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "edge"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The edge's ends one above the other.",
          "properties": {
            "edge": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "vertical",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "edge"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The two edges' chords parallel.",
          "properties": {
            "a": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "b": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "parallel",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "a",
            "b"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The two edges' chords at right angles.",
          "properties": {
            "a": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "b": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "perpendicular",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "a",
            "b"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "A smooth joint: the two contour edges meeting at the point leave it\nin opposite directions (no corner).",
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "const": "tangent",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "point": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "point"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "The two edges have the same length (along their curves).",
          "properties": {

            },

              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
            },

            "mm"

        {

            "kind": {
              "const": "length",

            "kind",
            "edge",

        {
          "additionalProperties": false,

              "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"

            "deg": {
              "description": "Degrees, 0–180.",
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            },
            "formula": {
              "description": "Computes `deg` from the body and the variables (a plain\nnumber).",
              "type": [
                "string",
                "null"
              ]
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "angle",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "a",
            "b",
            "deg"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",
      "pattern": "^point:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Add a constraint or a dimension.",
  "properties": {
    "constraint": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Constraint"
    },
    "measure": {
      "description": "For a dimension: keep the value the drawing has now (the one given\nis ignored).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "constraint"
  ],
  "title": "ConstraintAdd",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `point.set_smooth`

Make a contour point smooth (no corner: its two edges become curves whose handles line up, and stay so through a `tangent` constraint) or a corner again (the constraint is removed, the shape stays).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PointId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a point, e.g. `point:1`.",

      "type": "string"
    }
  },

  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Make a point smooth or a corner.",

    "point": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PointId"
    },
    "smooth": {
      "description": "`true`: the outline passes through the point without a corner (its\ntwo edges become curves with aligned handles, kept aligned by a\n`tangent` constraint); `false`: a corner again (the constraint goes,\nthe shape stays).",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [

    "smooth"

  "title": "PointSetSmooth",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.unfold`

Make a half piece whole and symmetric: it is unfolded across one of its straight edges (the axis, e.g. a centre front), which disappears. The other half follows every later change of the drawn half (points, curves, notches) and cannot be edited itself; seams and notches can go on it. panel.unlink makes the halves independent. Returns the new points and edges of the reflected half.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Unfold a half piece on one of its edges.",
  "properties": {
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId",
      "description": "A straight edge of the piece: the axis (a centre front on the fold)."
    },
    "panel": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "panel",
    "edge"
  ],
  "title": "PanelUnfold",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `panel.create_ellipse`

Create an elliptical (or, with equal radii, circular) panel: four curved edges between the points at the right, top, left and bottom. Returns the panel, then its 4 points, then its 4 edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create an elliptical panel.",
  "properties": {
    "centre": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Centre on the board, in mm. Defaults to `[0, 0]`.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "radii": {
      "description": "Half width and half height (mm, > 0); equal for a circle.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "radii"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateEllipse",
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `panel.create_sector`

Create an arc sector, the piece of a circle skirt: the inner arc is `inner_length_mm` long (the waist it covers), the outer arc `length_mm` further out (the hem), over `sweep_deg` (e.g. 180 for half a circle skirt). The radius comes from the waist: inner_length / sweep. The piece hangs below `centre`, its waist on top. Returns the panel, then its points (the hem from left to right, then the waist from right to left), then its edges.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Create an arc sector: a ring cut between two radii.",
  "properties": {
    "centre": {
      "default": [
        0.0,
        0.0
      ],
      "description": "Centre of the circles on the board (mm). Defaults to `[0, 0]`; the\npiece hangs below it.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "type": "array"
    },
    "grain_angle_deg": {
      "default": 90.0,
      "description": "Grainline angle in degrees from +X. Defaults to 90 (vertical).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "inner_length_mm": {
      "description": "Length of the inner arc (mm, > 0): the waist this piece covers.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "length_mm": {
      "description": "Distance from the inner to the outer arc (mm, > 0): the skirt's\nlength.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "Panel name. Defaults to \"Panel N\".",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sweep_deg": {
      "description": "The angle the piece covers (degrees, more than 0 and less than\n360): 180 for a half circle, 90 for a quarter. A full circle skirt\nis two half circles, or four quarters, sewn together.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "inner_length_mm",
    "length_mm",
    "sweep_deg"
  ],
  "title": "PanelCreateSector",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `edge.set_arc`

Make an edge a circular arc through its two ends, bulging `bulge_mm` from the straight line (positive outward). An arc over 90° is split into edges of at most 90° (new points between them); then the constraints on the edge are removed and its notches spread along the arc. Returns the new points and edges, if any.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "EdgeId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a edge, e.g. `edge:1`.",
      "pattern": "^edge:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Turn an edge into a circular arc.",
  "properties": {
    "bulge_mm": {
      "description": "How far the arc's middle is from the straight line between the\nedge's ends (mm, not 0): positive bulges outward (to the right of\nthe edge, as outlines turn counter-clockwise), negative inward.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "edge": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EdgeId"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "edge",
    "bulge_mm"
  ],
  "title": "EdgeSetArc",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `constraint.set_formula`

Give a dimension a formula of the body's measurements and the variables (e.g. "waist / 4 + 10 mm"): its value follows them, the drawing is redrawn when the body changes, and each size of the range is drafted with its own measurements (the points the formulas move are graded by them). Without `formula`, the dimension keeps its value. Errors say what is wrong: formula.syntax, formula.unknown_name, formula.cycle, formula.unit, formula.no_body, formula.domain, formula.range.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "ConstraintId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a constraint, e.g. `constraint:1`.",
      "pattern": "^constraint:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Give a dimension a formula, or take it away.",
  "properties": {
    "constraint": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ConstraintId"
    },
    "formula": {
      "description": "E.g. \"waist / 4 + 10 mm\", \"bust / 2 + ease\": arithmetic (+ - * /,\nparentheses, min, max, abs, sqrt) on numbers with units (mm, cm, m,\nin, deg), the body's measurements (height, bust, waist, hips) and\nvariables. A length for a distance or a length, a plain number\n(degrees) for an angle. Omitted: the dimension keeps its value and\nno longer follows the body.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "constraint"
  ],
  "title": "ConstraintSetFormula",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `variable.set`

Set a named variable that formulas can use (e.g. ease = "2 cm", dart = "(hips - waist) / 8"): created, or changed, and every formula using it follows.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json

  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

      "description": "Its formula, e.g. \"2 cm\" or \"bust / 20 + 5 mm\".",

    },
    "name": {
      "description": "A letter or _, then letters, digits or _ (not a body measurement,\na function or a unit).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "formula"
  ],
  "title": "VariableSet",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `variable.remove`

Remove a named variable; refused while a formula uses it (formula.unknown_name).

</details>

### `grading.check`

Check the grading in every size of the range: the seams (not gathered) whose two sides differ by more than `tolerance_mm` (default 1), with both lengths, and the pieces whose outline crosses itself. `ok` is true when no size has either.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Seams that no longer match in a size, and pieces that cross themselves.",
  "properties": {
    "tolerance_mm": {
      "description": "Report seams whose two sides differ by more than this (mm, default\n1).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "GradingCheck",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `grading.charts`

The built-in size charts for grading.use_chart: each chart's sizes with their bodies (cm).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The built-in size charts.",
  "title": "GradingCharts",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `constraint.list`

List the constraints and dimensions (on one piece, or all): each with its piece, its kind and what it names, a dimension's value and what the drawing measures now, whether it holds, and `marks` (where its points and the middles of its edges are, mm). `groups` are constraints sharing points, each with `freedom` (ways the constrained geometry can still move, moving or turning a piece as a whole included) and `redundant` constraints (over-constrained: they repeat what others say).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PanelId": {
      "description": "Identifier of a panel, e.g. `panel:1`.",
      "pattern": "^panel:[1-9][0-9]*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The constraints and dimensions, with how constrained the drawing is.",
  "properties": {
    "panel": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PanelId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Only those on this piece. Omitted: all of them."
    }
  },
  "title": "ConstraintList",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `guide.list`

List the construction lines: each with its ends `a` and `b` (mm).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The construction lines.",
  "title": "GuideList",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `variable.list`

List the named variables, each with its formula and its value in the size drawn (`mm` for a length, `number` otherwise; none while it needs a body the project does not have), and the body's measurements formulas can use (mm).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The named variables, with their values.",
  "title": "VariableList",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

## Actions

Operations that write files (not undoable). Paths are relative to the project folder and cannot leave it.

### `export.svg`

Export all panels as an SVG at 1:1 scale (cutting and sewing lines, notches, internal lines, grainlines, labels, 100 mm test square). With `sizes`, the pattern in those sizes of the range: one alone, or a graded nest (the base size in full, the others' cutting lines in colour with a legend). Returns the written path, relative to the project folder.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as SVG at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.svg`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportSvg",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `simulate`

Drape the placed and sewn panels on the avatar for a number of frames (1/60 s each, deterministic) and cache the result in the project, so `r3d render --view 3d` shows it. Returns the garment's extent, how open the seams are and whether the cloth has settled.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Drape the garment headless and cache the result.",
  "properties": {
    "frames": {
      "default": 300,
      "description": "Frames of 1/60 s to simulate (1–3600, default 300 = 5 s).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "title": "Simulate",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.pdf`

Export all panels as a PDF at 1:1 scale, tiled on A4/Letter pages (labelled A1, A2…, with overlap guides) or on one large page. Print at 100 % and check the 100 mm test square. With `sizes`, the pattern in those sizes of the range: one alone, or a graded nest. Returns the written path and page count.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "PaperSpec": {
      "description": "Page layout of a PDF export.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "a4",
          "description": "A4 tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "letter",
          "description": "US Letter tiles to print at home.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "single",
          "description": "One page as large as the pattern (plotter, print shop).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as a PDF at 1:1 scale.",
  "properties": {
    "paper": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/PaperSpec",
      "default": "a4",
      "description": "`a4` (default) or `letter` tiles with overlap and assembly guides,\nor `single` for one large page."
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.pdf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportPdf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.gltf`

Export the draped garment as glTF 2.0 binary (GLB): one named node and mesh per piece, metres, Y up, the pattern position as texture coordinates (1 unit = 1 m of fabric), the fabric as a PBR material with KHR_materials_sheen; the avatar too if asked. Uses the cached drape from `simulate` if it is up to date, otherwise the starting positions, and says which. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the draped garment as glTF 2.0 (GLB).",
  "properties": {
    "avatar": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include the avatar as its own node (default false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.glb`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportGltf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.obj`

Export the draped garment as Wavefront OBJ: one object per piece, metres, Y up, the pattern position as texture coordinates, smooth normals; geometry only. Uses the cached drape from `simulate` if it is up to date, otherwise the starting positions, and says which. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the draped garment as Wavefront OBJ.",
  "properties": {
    "avatar": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "Include the avatar as its own object (default false).",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.obj`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportObj",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `export.dxf`

Export all panels as DXF-AAMA (ASTM D6673, ASCII DXF in mm), for pattern and cutting software: one block per piece with its cutting line, sewing line, turn points, notches, grainline, internal lines and name. With `sizes`, a graded nest: every piece once per size, with a `Size:` text. Returns the written path.

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Export the pattern as DXF-AAMA.",
  "properties": {
    "path": {
      "description": "Output path relative to the project folder. Defaults to\n`exports/<project name>.dxf`.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "sizes": {
      "description": "Sizes of the range to export, by name: one size alone, or several\nnested (a graded nest). Default: the pattern as drawn (base size).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "ExportDxf",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `import.pattern`

Import the pieces of a pattern drawn elsewhere, from a DXF-AAMA (or plain DXF), SVG or PDF file inside the project folder: outlines (curves fitted back to editable edges), seam allowances, notches, grainlines, internal lines and names. A tiled PDF's pages are put back together. One undo step (`pattern.import`). Returns the new panels, what was left out, and the scale: `file`, `given` or `assumed` (check the size when assumed).

<details><summary>Parameters (JSON schema)</summary>

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "UnitSpec": {
      "description": "What one unit of an imported drawing is.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "mm",
            "cm",
            "m"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "in",
          "description": "Inch.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "pt",
          "description": "Point, 1/72 inch.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "px",
          "description": "CSS pixel, 1/96 inch.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "Import a pattern from a DXF-AAMA, SVG or PDF file.",
  "properties": {
    "page": {
      "description": "PDF: import only this page (1 = first). By default every page,\nwith the tiles of a tiled pattern put back together.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "path": {
      "description": "The file, relative to the project folder (`r3d import` and the app\ncopy files into `imports/`). Its extension gives the format:\n`.dxf`, `.svg` or `.pdf`.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "scale": {
      "description": "Size factor for a drawing at another scale (e.g. 2 for a pattern\ndrawn at half size). Default 1.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "units": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/UnitSpec"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "What one unit of the drawing is, when the file says nothing or says\nit wrong: `mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `pt` or `px`."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "path"
  ],
  "title": "ImportPattern",
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>
